presentation.label: DATA RHYTHM
presentation.summary: Data as rhythm on a MIDI track: the bits of pi, the primes, a cellular automaton or an LFSR, read as notes.
presentation.overview: DATAMATIC reads a stream of bits as a rhythm. The stream is one of nine: the binary digits of pi, e, the golden ratio or the square root of two, the Fibonacci word, the primes, the Thue-Morse sequence, an elementary cellular automaton (sixteen rules) or an LFSR. A window BITS wide slides along it STEP bits a step; a step plays when its window reaches the DENS threshold, so at DENS 0 with one bit the stream is the rhythm itself. The bits after each window choose its note (octave, fifth, tritone, whole-tone or semitone jumps over up to four octaves above the track's NOTE), its velocity and a late micro-timing. It writes ordinary note trigs with NOTE and VEL locks; the stock MIDI sequencer plays them at the pattern's tempo, track speed, length and swing. YES moves the window one byte along the stream for the next variation.
highlights: Nine data streams: four constants, three sequences, an automaton and an LFSR
A sliding bit window: width, stride and threshold shape the density
Octave, fifth, tritone, whole-tone and semitone jumps; velocity and micro-timing from the data
Real trigs and locks: edit any step as usual; no clock of its own
usage: On a MIDI track double-tap SRC for MIDI NOTE SETUP, choose DATAMAT in the list on the left and press YES.
The SRC page holds SRCE, OFFS, BITS, DENS and the base note (OCT, ROOT); the AMP page SPRD, INTV, VDAT, JITR, VEL and LEN; FUNC+AMP RULE, SEED and STEP.
Every turn rewrites the track; YES reads the next byte of the stream. For fast data rhythms set the track's speed to 2x or 4x.

controls.name: SRCE
controls.doc: SRC A. The stream: PI, E, PHI and SQR2 (binary digits), FIBO (Fibonacci word), PRIM (primes), THUE (Thue-Morse), CA (cellular automaton), LFSR

controls.name: OFFS
controls.doc: SRC B. Where the window starts, in bytes into the stream; YES moves it to the next byte

controls.name: BITS
controls.doc: SRC C. The window's width in bits, 1-8

controls.name: DENS
controls.doc: SRC D. 0 plays a step whose window is all ones (with BITS 1 the stream itself), 127 plays every step

controls.name: SPRD
controls.doc: AMP A. Octaves the notes may reach above the track's NOTE, 0-4

controls.name: INTV
controls.doc: AMP B. The intervals the notes jump by: OCT, 5TH, TRIT (tritones), WHOL (whole tones), CLST (semitones)

controls.name: VDAT
controls.doc: AMP C. How far the data pulls velocity below the track's VEL (OFF: every note at VEL)

controls.name: JITR
controls.doc: AMP D. Micro-timing from the data, at most this many 1/24 of a step late (OFF: on the grid)

controls.name: SEED
controls.doc: FUNC+AMP B. The automaton's first row (0: one live cell) and the LFSR's start

controls.name: STEP
controls.doc: FUNC+AMP C. Bits the window moves each step, 1-8; below BITS the windows overlap

limitations: Needs the Modwerk base loaded over USB (beta) with the MIDI generators (ot_midi_generators). Card firmware cannot include it.
One trig a step: for denser data rhythms raise the track's speed. Micro-timing is late only, 0 to 23/24 of a step.
The streams are the first 2048 bits of each table and 64 rows of the automaton; OFFS reaches 1016 bits in.
It takes the MIDI track's SRC and AMP pages (and FUNC+AMP) and keeps the arpeggiator off there; choosing it sets the track's NOTE to C4 (48), VEL to 100 and NOT2-4 off.
Not yet run on hardware or in the emulator.

storage.label: Storage
storage.conditions: From the USB package build.py makes from the sources (m68k-elf-gcc 16.2, -Os): 6,936 bytes of ColdFire code and data (1,792 of them the seven stream tables) and 1,004 of bss, one instance, 113 relocations, no stock-code sites. No DSP memory, no heap.

processing.label: CPU load
processing.conditions: Work happens on the UI task once per knob turn or YES: a stream of 2048 bits, a 64-step line and an in-place rewrite of the track record. Nothing runs while the pattern plays.

impact.conditions: A knob turn or YES on a DATAMATIC track; idle otherwise.

cpu.rationale: One 2048-bit stream (at most 64 automaton rows of 32 cells), one 64-step line and an in-place record rewrite per edit on the UI task; nothing at interrupt level and nothing while playing.

dsp.rationale: No DSP code and no change to the DSP programs.

memory.rationale: 7,940 bytes of ColdFire code, data and state in DRAM (6,936 + 1,004 from the package header); the line it writes is the track's own record.

tests.summary: Host checks only: the stream tables hold pi, the primes, Thue-Morse and the Fibonacci word and regenerate byte for byte; the automaton follows each of its sixteen rules; DENS 0 plays the stream and DENS 127 every step; 20,000 random settings give deterministic lines inside their octaves, velocities and micro-timing; the MIDI record writer (test_engine.py, under the sanitizers); the package's generator record sits at the registry's index. Not run on a unit or in the emulator.

license.declaration: Original work. The data streams are mathematical constants and sequences computed by generate_tables.py; the generator glue follows the shape of VECTOR 0.3.0's MIT midi.c. No Elektron firmware, extracted routines, tables, samples or dumps are included.

access.location: MIDI track: MIDI NOTE SETUP (double-tap SRC), DATAMAT in the list on the left
steps: Press MIDI, select a MIDI track, double-tap SRC, UP/DOWN to DATAMAT in the list on the left and press YES.
SRC holds SRCE, OFFS, BITS, DENS, OCT and ROOT; AMP holds SPRD, INTV, VDAT, JITR, VEL and LEN; FUNC+AMP holds RULE, SEED and STEP. Hold a trig for stock's page and its locks.
